english_delivery_scope: fully_english. The University of Brescia describes the Bachelor's Degree course in Business and Economics as entirely in English and based in Brescia, active from academic year 2025/2026. It is listed on the university's 'Study programmes taught in English' page as the English-taught bachelor's programme in the Economics Area. All teaching, the entrance test (CEnT-S / English TOLC-E) and the language requirement (English B2) are configured for an English-medium programme, and non-EU candidates are exempted from the Italian language test precisely because the programme is entirely taught in English. The programme totals 180 CFU over three years.
programme_status: active_first_year. The programme is newly activated from academic year 2025/2026 (the official course page is labelled 'Business and Economics - New A.Y. 25/26') and is actively recruiting first-year students for 2026/2027, with an enrolment window running 13 July - 17 December 2026. It is an open-access (free access) programme with no numerus clausus, so no cap-based selection applies and there is no phasing-out restriction on new applications.
pre_evaluation_required: No dedicated PICA pre-evaluation is documented for this bachelor's programme. The University of Brescia's PICA-based pre-assessment procedure explicitly addresses non-EU candidates living abroad applying to master's (second-cycle) degrees, with a first round closing 15 March 2026 at noon Italian time; the university's undergraduate pages do not describe an equivalent PICA pre-evaluation for bachelor's degrees. Instead, non-EU candidates living abroad follow the standard route: a study-visa / pre-enrolment application submitted through the Universitaly portal (deadline 31 August 2026), plus submission of qualification documents to the International Students Office. [uncertain]
entry_test_name: CEnT-S (CISIA English Test - Sciences), delivered by CISIA; this is the renamed successor of the English TOLC-E (Test Online CISIA per l'Economia, English-language version), and University of Brescia pages still use both names for the same requirement (the page at www.unibs.it/en/EnglishTOLC-E is titled 'Test CEnT-S - Business and Economics'). The test is compulsory but NON-SELECTIVE and purely orientative: it does not rank or exclude candidates, and a poor result does not prevent enrolment. Only the 'Mathematics' section counts for enrolment purposes; candidates may also sit 'Reasoning on texts and data', but that section's result is not taken into consideration. A score of at least 4/13 in Mathematics allows enrolment without Additional Educational Obligations (OFA); below that threshold, or without sitting the test at all, an OFA in Mathematics is assigned. The test may be retaken at any CISIA-member university, even after enrolment, no later than 25 October, to clear the Mathematics OFA. It can be sat on university premises or in TOLC@CASA (home-testing) mode.
admission_type: open access (free access / accesso libero) with a compulsory but non-selective CISIA entrance test (CEnT-S / English TOLC-E). There is no numerus clausus and no ranking-based selection; the test only determines whether an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA) in Mathematics is assigned.
academic_requirements: A secondary school diploma (Italian upper-secondary leaving qualification) or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad and recognised as suitable under current Italian legislation. The programme comprises 180 CFU over three years, with 56 CFU in the first year across four main subject areas plus a Digital Skills lab (2 CFU) and a foreign language course. Mathematical prerequisites are verified through the compulsory CEnT-S / English TOLC-E entrance test: at least 4/13 in the Mathematics section avoids an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA) in Mathematics. An insufficient Mathematics result does not block enrolment or class attendance; it only assigns the OFA, which must subsequently be cleared. Applicants with foreign qualifications must have their qualification assessed for suitability by the International Students Office.
language_requirements: English at CEFR level B2 is a mandatory entry requirement, evidenced by one of the certifications approved by the Department (CCSA - the course's joint teaching committee). Alternative routes to satisfy the B2 requirement: (1) exemption for students who have completed an entire study programme delivered in English; (2) exemption for native English speakers from designated countries; (3) exemption for students who attended a Foundation Year course taught in English; (4) sitting the CLA-Unibs B2 English level test, a dedicated in-house option reserved for students enrolling on the Business and Economics programme who need English B2 but do not hold any of the admitted certifications. The CLA B2 test consists of written and oral parts, is held in person in a computer lab on the Moodle platform, runs across six scheduled sessions per year, and on success yields an 'Attestazione CLA livello B2' issued as an Open Badge. Italian language proficiency is NOT required: non-EU candidates are exempted from the Italian language test because the degree programme is entirely taught in English.
application_deadline_eu: Enrolment window 13 July 2026 - 17 December 2026 (for candidates who sat the CEnT-S in 2025 or 2024, on university premises or in TOLC@CASA mode). Requests for tuition-fee exemption/reduction must also be submitted by 17 December 2026. The Mathematics OFA can be cleared by re-sitting the test no later than 25 October.
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU candidates resident abroad must submit and complete their study-visa / pre-enrolment request on the Universitaly portal by 31 August 2026, selecting University of Brescia and this programme; the university enrolment window itself remains 13 July - 17 December 2026. This Universitaly visa deadline is separate from, and earlier than, the general enrolment deadline, and must not be conflated with it. (The 15 March 2026 noon PICA pre-assessment deadline applies to master's degrees, not to this bachelor's programme.) [uncertain]
required_documents: Secondary school diploma / foreign upper-secondary qualification; academic transcripts/certificates; proof of English at CEFR B2 (an approved certification, an exemption document, or the CLA-Unibs B2 attestation); CEnT-S / English TOLC-E result. For candidates holding foreign qualifications: documents legalised by the competent foreign authorities or bearing the Apostille stamp, plus either a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the Italian diplomatic representation or, as an alternative, a CIMEA Statement of Comparability; where required, a CIMEA Statement of Verification may substitute for legalisation. CIMEA statements are obtained via the Diplome online platform. The university recommends uploading diploma and certificates in Italian, French or English to speed up evaluation. International students must book an appointment with the International Students Office to submit these documents. Non-EU candidates abroad additionally need the Universitaly pre-enrolment/visa application. No Italian language test certificate is required for this programme.
entry_exam_or_test: Compulsory, non-selective, orientative entrance test: CEnT-S (CISIA English Test - Sciences), the successor name of the English-language TOLC-E, administered in English by CISIA. It is a computer-based test that can be taken at any CISIA-consortium university providing it, either on university premises or from home in TOLC@CASA mode. The full CEnT-S comprises 5 sections and 55 questions in total (including a 5-question Physics section), but for Business and Economics only the 'Mathematics' section is evaluated for enrolment; the 'Reasoning on texts and data' section may optionally be completed but its result is not taken into account. Purpose: to assess whether the candidate's basic mathematics preparation is adequate for the programme. Outcome: at least 4/13 in Mathematics means enrolment with no Additional Educational Obligation (OFA); a lower score, or not sitting the test, results in an OFA in Mathematics being assigned. The test does not rank, exclude, or cap candidates. Results from tests sat in 2024 or 2025 are valid for the 2026 enrolment window. Retakes are permitted at any CISIA university, including after enrolment, up to 25 October. No interview or personal-preparation assessment is required.

source_quotes.quote: The Bachelor's Degree course in Business and Economics is entirely in English and based in Brescia.
A B2 level English proficiency according to the CEFR must be demonstrated by possession of one of the certifications approved by the CCSA.

Enrolment in the degree of Business and Economics is open from 13th July to 17th December 2026, for those who took CEnT-S - whether on the university premises or in TOLC@CASA (home-testing) mode - in 2025 or 2024.
The English TOLC-E aptitude test is orientative and non-selective; its purpose is to evaluate whether the basic mathematics preparation is adequate.

You must complete the section 'Mathematics' of the CEnT-S; you may also complete the section 'Reasoning on texts and data', but the result of this section will not be taken into consideration for enrolment purposes.
You can enrol without Additional Educational Requirements (OFAs) if you scored at least 4/13 in Mathematics.

These tests are reserved for students enrolling on the Bachelor of Business and Economics degree programme and need English B2 as an entry requirement but do not hold any of the admitted certifications.
If the degree programme is entirely taught in English, candidates are exempted from the Italian language test.
Candidates living in non-EU areas must submit and complete their requests for study visa in Universitaly portal by 31 August 2026.
Declaration of value prepared by Italian Representation or alternatively the Statement of comparability issued by CIMEA.
Course teaching secretariat U.O.C. Economics Educational Services, Department of Economics and Management, Via S. Faustino 74/B Brescia.

uncertainty_notes:
ACCESS LIMITATION (primary caveat): unibs.it and corsi.unibs.it are protected by a Cloudflare/human-verification bot challenge. Direct retrieval failed on every attempt - WebFetch returned HTTP 405 for https://corsi.unibs.it/en/business-economics and HTTP 403 for https://www.unibs.it/en/cds-business-economics, https://www.unibs.it/en/education/enrolling/matriculating/bachelors-degree-courses/business-and-economics and for unibs.it-hosted PDFs. A real browser session loaded only a 'Human Verification / Let's confirm you are human' interstitial; the challenge was deliberately NOT completed (bypassing bot detection is out of scope). All content below was therefore compiled from search-engine indexed snippets of those same official unibs.it / corsi.unibs.it pages, and NO page was directly verified. Field values should be re-checked against the live pages before publication.

SPECIFIC UNCERTAINTIES:
1. degree_class: Indexed content places Business and Economics in class L-18 (Science of Business Administration), while the sibling Economics and Data Analysis programme is L-33. Because the programme name and economics orientation could also suggest L-33, and the L-18 attribution came from a single indexed snippet of the didactic regulations PDF (B&E Regolamento didattico) rather than a directly verified page, L-18 is marked uncertain.
2. entry_test_name naming: Sources use 'CEnT-S', 'English TOLC-E' and 'TOLC-E ENGLISH' interchangeably. CEnT-S (CISIA English Test - Sciences) appears to be the current CISIA name replacing English TOLC-E, and the unibs page at /en/EnglishTOLC-E is titled 'Test CEnT-S - Business and Economics', which supports them being the same requirement. However the university's own pages are inconsistent, and one indexed snippet describes CEnT-S as a 5-section, 55-question science test including Physics - a structure that reads more like a science test than an economics test. Candidates should confirm the exact current test code with CISIA and the department.
3. pre_evaluation_required: All located PICA pre-assessment material at unibs.it is explicitly scoped to master's/second-cycle degrees (first round closing 15 March 2026, noon). No undergraduate PICA pre-evaluation page was found, so the conclusion that none is required for this bachelor's programme is an inference from absence of evidence, not a positive confirmation. There is a STAR scholarship call for bachelor's applicants from non-EU countries that does use PICA, but that is a grant application, not an admission pre-evaluation.
4. application_deadline_non_eu: The 31 August 2026 Universitaly study-visa deadline is a university-wide non-EU deadline, not one confirmed on the Business and Economics programme page itself. Non-EU applicants should treat the Universitaly visa deadline and the 13 July - 17 December 2026 enrolment window as two separate obligations.
5. Deadline year consistency: Multiple indexed snippets give '13th July to 17th December 2026'. Because the programme launched in 2025/2026 and the current date is September 2026, this window most plausibly refers to enrolment for a.y. 2026/2027, but the academic year is not stated explicitly in the retrieved snippets.
6. required_documents: Compiled from the university's general international-admissions and CIMEA pages rather than a programme-specific checklist; the exact document set for this programme should be confirmed with the International Students Office.
7. campus: Brescia is confirmed; the specific teaching venue (Via San Faustino 74/B) is the Department of Economics and Management address given as the course teaching secretariat contact, which is the normal teaching location but was not separately confirmed as the lecture venue.
8. tuition_or_fees_link: Points to the general university fees page; no programme-specific fee schedule for Business and Economics was located. Note the 2026/2027 fee regulations extend the 'no tax' exemption threshold to an ISEE of EUR 28,000, with further reductions at higher ISEE bands.
